clue.text: Yanks' stupid people

definitions.meaning: yanks are sudden sharp pulls, the plural verb or noun sense
fools or idiots, in the American slang sense

explanation.definitionFit: A jerk is a sharp tug and also, in American slang, a contemptible fool, so both senses share one plural word.

clue.text: The man's a fool — he stuck to a fat-free diet

definitions.text: he stuck to a fat-free diet

parts.note: Jack is a generic man, so the man's is Jack's
a prat is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot boasts of following a strict low-fat diet.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme this figure could eat no fat while his wife could eat no lean.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme character famously ate only lean meat, a man who avoided grease entirely.

clue.text: After drinking port, small individual is seen to act without restraint

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the port goes inside the small individual

parts.note: a runt is an undersized animal or person
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A little chap downs some port and is seen to let himself go.
explanation.definitionFit: To run riot is to behave wildly and unchecked, an idiom for unrestrained conduct.

clue.text: Burst of applause for saving clause

definitions.meaning: a round of cheering, a sudden outburst of clapping
a legal reservation or proviso in a contract

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a volley of cheers and a reservation or proviso, an old legal sense.

clue.text: Landing right one, chap married. When? Armistice Day

annotationWithheld.why: Landing right one, chap married. When? Armistice Day (9): M (married) + AS (when) is clear, but no sound reading of 'Landing right one, chap' gives MARTIN
annotationWithheld.clue: Landing right one, chap married. When? Armistice Day

clue.text: Picketing court, stubborn chap finally arrested and fined

indicators.note: pickets stand around a place, so the stubborn chap surrounds the court

parts.note: a mule is an obstinate person

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of arrested

explanation.surface: A stubborn protester picketing a law court is arrested and penalised.
explanation.definitionFit: To mulct is to penalise by a money penalty, so the past tense means charged a fine.

clue.text: Go back and provide further therapy

definitions.meaning: to withdraw or retire from a position

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to withdraw, and split as re-treat it means to give medical care once more.

clue.text: Where those who walked the plank finished, usually

definitions.text: Where those who walked the plank finished
definitions.meaning: the main is the open sea, where pirates' victims fell

explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic word for the ocean, and the idiom means mostly or on the whole.

clue.text: Acceptable behaviour monarch drummed into wife

indicators.note: drummed into means forced inside, so the monarch is put within the wife

parts.note: Mrs is the title of a married woman
Queen Anne, British monarch 1702 to 1714

explanation.surface: A king or queen hammers good conduct into a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Good manners are polite social conduct, the etiquette expected of people.

clue.text: The way pictures open

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
pictures are art

explanation.surface: This is how films begin.
explanation.definitionFit: To start something is to begin or open it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: With very poor light, a hundred and fifty elect not to finish

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: not to finish means the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: the elect, the chosen few, are an elite

explanation.surface: A hundred and fifty people chosen to lead decide against completing their term, all in gloomy light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to finish' trims ELITE to ELIT. 'elect' looks like a verb but is a noun, the chosen.
explanation.definitionFit: A room lit only by tapers is dim, so the adjective describes a scene with feeble illumination.

clue.text: Indian vehicle used in Polynesian island

definitions.meaning: a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage used in India
a kingdom of islands in the South Pacific

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a horse-drawn cart of the subcontinent and a Pacific island kingdom.

clue.text: Reduce the speed for this form of transport

indicators.note: reduce in its chemical sense of breaking down, so these words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An instruction to slow down suits some vehicle or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduce' looks like an order to slow down, but it signals the anagram of all of THE SPEED FOR THIS; 'for this' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The camel earned this nickname as the desert's beast of burden, carrying goods and riders like a vessel.

clue.text: About worn out, went to bed

parts.note: re means about or concerning
worn out means exhausted, tired

explanation.surface: Someone exhausted turned in for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire for the night is to go off to sleep, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Bird disposed to linger, gulping unfinished drink

indicators.note: gulping means swallowing, so the drink goes inside the rearranged letters
disposed means arranged or set out, so the letters of linger are rearranged
unfinished means the last letter of the drink is dropped

parts.note: ouzo is a Greek aniseed spirit

explanation.surface: A bird inclined to hang about swallows a half-finished drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is the definition, not part of the surface's subject; 'disposed' makes RINGEL from linger, 'gulping' takes the drink in, and 'unfinished' docks its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This thrush of upland Britain, with a white crescent on its breast, is a species of bird.

clue.text: Time to redeem something seen in the window

parts.note: to ransom a captive is to redeem them by payment

explanation.surface: A pawnbroker's customer finally reclaims an item displayed in the shop window.
explanation.definitionFit: This crosspiece or the small pane above a door is part of a window's structure.

clue.text: Decrepit doctor with no right to be menacing

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: with no means the letter for right is left out

parts.note: to threaten is to be menacing

explanation.surface: A frail physician has no business being threatening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes R from THREATEN, leaving THEATEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing eaten by larvae is ragged and shabby, so the word means worn out or dilapidated.

clue.text: Liner with strong man in charge

parts.note: a titan is a giant of great strength

explanation.surface: An ocean ship captained by a powerful figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous ocean steamship that sank in 1912 was a passenger vessel of the White Star Line.

clue.text: Best-known agents casting English or Greek tragedian

indicators.note: casting means throwing off, so the letter for English is discarded

parts.note: the spies, with stressed the, are the pre-eminent secret agents

explanation.surface: The top talent agency is casting an English or Greek tragic actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casting' looks like a theatrical audition, but it means shedding the E from THE SPIES. 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Thespis of Icaria is held to be the first actor and the father of Greek drama.

clue.text: Manpower reduced in the barbering job?

parts.note: a crew is a team of workers, manpower
reduced means cut

explanation.surface: Staff have been cut at the barber's.
explanation.definitionFit: A short bristly haircut is a style a barber produces.

clue.text: Nought's amiss in range

indicators.note: amiss means out of order, so the letters are put wrong

explanation.surface: A zero has gone astray somewhere in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Nought's supplies an S here: the fodder is NOUGHTS, seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Within gunshot means within the distance a firearm can reach, so the word means shooting distance.

clue.text: Well covered in blood, become distraught

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped round, so the well sits inside the blood

parts.note: gore is spilt blood
a spa is a mineral spring or well

explanation.surface: Someone drenched in blood would understandably be upset.
explanation.walkthrough: GO SPARE is British slang for getting furious or frantic.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means to lose one's temper or go frantic with worry.

clue.text: He had to get excited

indicators.note: get excited means stirred up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone simply had to lose his cool.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: an impetuous person is one who must get worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: An impetuous rash person is quick to become worked up, so the clue sketches one.

clue.text: Exponents of authority

parts.note: exponents are powers in mathematics, and those who wield authority are the established rulers

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names those who hold control in an organisation or state, the people in charge.

clue.text: Emblem displayed by child upset me

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

explanation.surface: A small child shows a badge that unsettles the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ME into EM. 'displayed by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a symbol or object revered as the emblem of a clan.

clue.text: I kept away from beautiful women during the time appointed for work

indicators.note: kept away from means the letter I is removed from the women

parts.note: houris are beautiful maidens of the Muslim paradise

explanation.surface: The speaker avoided attractive company during working time.
explanation.definitionFit: Office hours are the set period of the working day, so the plural means the shift.

clue.text: Gem has to go back

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back means the word for going is read in reverse

parts.note: to zap is to go quickly, to zip

explanation.surface: A jewel must be returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ZAP to PAZ. 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellowish precious stone is a classic jewel, often the November birthstone.

clue.text: Given to intemperance, turn place into a tip

indicators.note: made into a tip, a mess, means the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker trashes the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'into a tip', a British phrase for a filthy mess, does the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Crapulent describes someone sick from overindulgence in drink, a drunken excess.

clue.text: It let some get carried away at Christmas

definitions.text: It let some get carried away at Christmas

indicators.note: carried away means swept off, so the letters are moved out of their order

explanation.surface: Something at Christmas time lets a few people lose their inhibitions.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: couples under this sprig are licensed to kiss at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The festive sprig hung at Christmas licenses kissing beneath it, so people get carried away.

clue.text: American car, an outmoded form of transport

definitions.meaning: in the US a saloon car is so called
a ... chair, carried on poles by two bearers

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a closed saloon car in the US and the enclosed chair once borne by porters.
